title.raw: Table beet harvest yield per hectare; yield range and its influencing factors
title.rendered: Table beet harvest yield per hectare; yield range and its influencing factors

content.raw:
Answer to the main question: Has performance been reported per hectare?

Based on the available university extension source, commercial table beet yield data on a hectare scale is not available. This source is a home gardening guide that reports crop yield only on a small-scale home garden basis.Source.

Therefore, the direct answer to your inquiry is: there is no recorded yield per hectare for table beets in the cited source. All observations presented relate to home gardening conditions in the state of Utah, United States.

Documented performance range at the small farm scale

Fresh table beet yield under home garden conditions varies depending on different varieties and reaches maturity within sixty to eighty days after planting.Source.

Documented yield observations are reported as follows:

  • Fresh root yield: five to ten pounds per ten feet of planted row length
  • Maturity time range: sixty to eighty days from planting

These figures relate solely to home-scale conditions and no data has been derived from them for conversion or generalization to commercial performance per hectare.Source.

Documented factors affecting yield

Three key factors affecting table beet performance have been identified based on university observations, each reported qualitatively:

  • Water stress during the first six weeks:Water stress in the first to sixth week after planting often leads to premature flowering and reduced yield.Source.
  • Soil moisture fluctuations:Sudden changes in soil moisture cause root cracking, reduced leaf growth, and yield loss.Source.
  • Crop variety:Time to maturity and final yield vary depending on the selected variety.Source.

Summary table of documented observations

Factor Type of effect Stage / Conditions Reported scale
Early water stress Reduced yield First to sixth week after planting Home / Small farm
Soil moisture fluctuation Root cracking and yield reduction Growing season duration Home / Small farm
Time to maturity Yield range Sixty to eighty days from planting Home / Small farm
Fresh root yield Five to ten pounds Per ten feet of row length Home / Small farm

Application and limitations of results

The present results are interpretable only within the geographic domain of Utah state and home garden conditions. The lack of multiple independent sources limits the statistical credibility of the performance range to a single university observation.Source.

No guaranteed figures, commercial performance rates, Iranian cultivation recommendations, or local planting calendar have been derived from this source. All units are reported in accordance with the original source (pounds and feet of row), and converting them to metric is the responsibility of the publisher's rendering layer, not this article.

Source limitations:University extension unit (Utah State University Extension) with a geographic scope limited to Utah state; aimed at home gardening guidance; lacking commercial performance data on a hectare scale; impossibility of generalization to Iranian conditions; absence of independent multi-source confirmation.

Prepared with AI assistance and university sources; not a substitute for local field assessment and professional advice.

Frequently asked questions

Is table beet yield data per hectare available?

No. The cited source is a home gardening guide and lacks commercial performance data on a hectare scale.

What is the home-scale table beet yield?

Under home garden conditions, fresh root yield has been reported as five to ten pounds per ten feet of planted row length.

What factors affect table beet yield?

Water stress during the first six weeks of growth, soil moisture fluctuations, and crop variety are among the factors affecting yield and root quality.
